newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end higher in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end higher in quiet trade.

text.p: The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended higher on Monday in quiet trade, after being boosted in the morning by a rise in U.S. Treasuries on Friday.
Investors were quiet for most of the day, traders said.
"There weren't any significant moves by investors today," a trader for a brokerage house said.
The rise in the March was puzzling in view of investors' inactivity, he added.
The March ended at 125.30, up from Friday's 125.05.
Investors were detected buying long-term cash JGBs in the morning, but otherwise things were quiet, a trader for a long-term credit bank said.
In the morning, JGBs were supported by a rise in U.S. Treasuries on Friday, and firmer Tokyo share prices, the trader at the long-term credit bank said.
A rise in Tokyo stocks caused buying back by dealers who had felt that a decline in stock prices would lead to profit-taking selling of JGBs, he said.
The 6-1/2 percent 30-year benchmark U.S. Treasury bond ended up 20/32 at 99-00 on Friday.
JGBs were stuck in a tight range during the day, as buying demand was detected on the downside, and selling was expected to emerge on the upperside, traders said.
"Selling is expected to appear at around 125.30 to 125.50, and buying is likely to support JGBs at below 125.10," the second trader said.
The expectation that investors will sell on highs was making it difficult to make aggressive tries for the upperside, a trader for a trust bank's securities affiliate said.
Such selling by investors was not seen on Monday, however, the brokerage house trader said.
The benchmark 182nd JGB's yield stood at 2.430 percent as of 0707 GMT, down from Friday's 2.455 percent.
Market players said they expect the U.S. Fed's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee to leave interest rates unchanged, at its scheduled meeting on Tuesday.
Movements in the U.S. stock and bond markets after the FOMC will be closely watched, traders said.
The agreement by the World Trade Organisation at its ministerial conference on Friday to further liberalise world trade was virtually ignored by Japan's bond market.
